name: Facial icing with green tea ice cubes
lead: Facial icing with green tea ice cubes is a social media skincare practice in which frozen brewed green tea is rubbed on the face, with proponents citing reduced puffiness and calmer skin.

No studies found on this practice. Wikipedia describes general cold therapy as agreed to relieve symptoms like swelling with study results that conflict, and notes that green tea compounds have no proven biological effects in humans [1][2].

paras: Practitioners brew green tea, freeze it in trays and apply the cubes to the face, often in the morning, in the belief that cold plus tea antioxidants reduce redness and puffiness.
No studies found. Studies of ice packs on injuries report short-term pain relief, with limited long-term evidence [1]. Adverse events from cold therapy are suspected to be underreported [1].

General cold therapy sources note frostbite risk with extreme cold and listed contraindications such as Raynaud syndrome and poor circulation or sensation [1]. Green tea extracts can cause skin reactions in some people [2].

card.summary: Rubbing frozen green tea on the face for de-puffing; untested for this use.
card.note: Avoid prolonged ice contact with skin.

quick.overview:
A TikTok-popularised routine of applying frozen green tea to the face.

No study has tested it; general cold therapy research concerns injuries.
quick.mechanism: Cold constricts blood vessels and slows flow locally; green tea adds polyphenols whose human effects are unproven [1][2].
quick.risks: Ice burns and skin irritation are possible; circulation disorders are listed contraindications for cold therapy [1].
